I am a 62-year-old farmer with a high education level and 40 years of experience. I farm 8 mu in Quzhou County with my wife, running a wheat-maize double-cropping system. Let me think through my plan for this year.

**My reasoning:**

Forty years on this land means I know every plot. With my education, I understand nutrient management and crop physiology, but I am still a smallholder — just two of us, limited cash, and every yuan matters. I target yields of around 450 kg/mu for wheat and 500 kg/mu for maize, which is realistic with decent weather.

For **winter wheat**, I plant in early October (around October 8) with an improved semi-dwarf variety. I apply a base fertilizer of compound fertilizer before planting — about 10 kg N, 8 kg P₂O₅, and 5 kg K₂O per mu — then topdress with 8 kg N per mu at jointing in March if the stand looks good. I irrigate three times: winter irrigation in late November, jointing stage in spring, and heading stage. I use herbicide once in spring. With only two of us, I hire a custom operator for sowing and combine harvesting, but we handle spreading fertilizer and irrigation ourselves.

For **summer maize**, the turnaround after wheat harvest is brutally tight — usually 5–7 days. I harvest wheat around June 10, shred the straw, and plant hybrid maize by June 14. I apply all fertilizer at planting — about 15 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 4 kg K₂O per mu — because there is no time for split application in this system. I irrigate immediately after planting for emergence, and once more at tasseling if rainfall is insufficient. Labor is tight, so I hire help for the rapid wheat harvest and maize planting sequence.

I am slightly conservative on nitrogen this year — not because I don't know the optimal rate, but because input prices have been high and at my scale, the risk of cash shortage matters more than chasing the last 5% of yield. I would rather under-apply slightly than run out of money for the maize season.
